panels.rationale: Single-panel plain radiograph of both hands from an RS3PE case report. Caption and in-text confirm soft tissue swelling, extensor tenosynovitis, and synovitis without bone erosion in a patient diagnosed with RS3PE syndrome, matching the nonerosive polyarthritis radiographic pattern classic for RS3PE. No third-party copyright indicated; prior triage kept the figure.

panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a real patient showing bilateral pitting dorsal hand edema with symmetrical synovitis of the wrists and MCP joints; the caption explicitly attributes the presentation to RS3PE syndrome ('Clinical presentation of RS3PE syndrome. Bilateral pitting edema of the hands with symmetrical synovitis involving the wrists and metacarpophalangeal joints'), matching the classic boxing-glove hand edema phenotype. Prior caption triage also classified it as a real patient RS3PE clinical photo with no third-party indication. Skin is adequately lit and shows medium tone with chronic sun-damaged elderly hands; no ethnicity or specific patient age stated in caption or in-text, so ethnicity is null and age group is inferred as older adult from visible elderly hands plus in-text statement that RS3PE typically affects elderly individuals.

in_text_mentions: RS3PE is a rare inflammatory syndrome typically affecting elderly individuals and characterized by symmetrical synovitis and pitting edema of the hands. It has been associated with various malignancies, highlighting the importance of malignancy screening in these patients [4,5]. Clinical findings are demonstrated in Figure 4.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Clinical photograph of the right hand showing dorsal pitting edema, the hallmark boxing-glove edema of RS3PE; caption and in-text explicitly attribute the hand/foot pitting edema to the RS3PE syndrome in this case report. Desquamation is also visible but is noted in-text as a TSS feature, so it is listed only as a proposed finding. b: Clinical photograph of the left hand showing symmetric dorsal pitting edema, the classic boxing-glove presentation of RS3PE, explicitly captioned as pitting edema of the left hand in this RS3PE case report. Desquamation is also visible but is a TSS-associated feature per in-text, so recorded only as a proposed finding. c: Clinical photograph of the dorsum of the right foot with a red circle highlighting pitting edema with remaining indentation, a classic RS3PE manifestation; caption and in-text attribute the hand and foot pitting edema to the RS3PE syndrome. Red-circle annotation present.
